inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E (year ending 2026-10-31) = midpoint of the 19-Aug-2026 guidance range $3,035-3,075M; 9M actual $2,228.0M (XBRL RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax), implied Q4 $807-847M against Q3 actual $817.7M and backlog +35% YoY.
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted: 55.699M common shares on the Q3 FY2026 10-Q cover (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding, 2026-08-18) + 0.313M dilutive share-based awards (us-gaap:IncrementalCommonSharesAttributableToShareBasedPaymentArrangements, quarter to 2026-07-31) = 56.01M. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging both dilution and the expense would double-count.
inputs.total_debt_note: At 2026-07-31: commercial paper 192.0 + current maturities of long-term debt 10.0 + long-term debt 1,529.0 = 1,731.0 (us-gaap:LongTermDebt ties to 1,731.005) + finance lease liabilities 18.7 (current 9.9 + non-current 8.8). The Metrics CSV carries 1,741.0, which double-counts the $10.0M current portion (same defect as the FCX/KEYS DB rows); the XBRL components are used here. Operating lease liabilities (68.5) are deliberately excluded - see lease_treatment.
inputs.interest_income_note: TTM interest income is $2.2M (us-gaap:InvestmentIncomeInterest). Not stripped: Nordson is a net-DEBT company (net debt 2.3x owner FCF), so there is no cash pile being double-counted in the bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation cash-flow add-back, TTM to 2026-07-31 (FY2025 18.944 - 9M FY2025 13.255 + 9M FY2026 17.512). No separate equity-award tax-withholding line is tagged in the XBRL (PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation absent; treasury purchases 306.4 = repurchases 306.4 in FY2025), so sbc_incl_equity_taxes equals the add-back. At 0.8% of revenue the omission is immaterial (<0.1% of revenue if withholding runs at a third of SBC).
inputs.buyback_cash_note: FY2025 cash repurchases (us-gaap:PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock); 9M FY2026 158.8. Diluted share count has fallen 57.6M (FY2024) -> 56.0M, so the flat count is funded by the repurchaser, not a modelling convention. Buybacks beyond the SBC offset are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-01T20:00:01Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API, regularMarketTime); 52-week range 223.29-339.12
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate: 10y UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.05-1.10 = cost of equity ~9.5-9.7%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.3% (FY2025 interest paid 98.7 on ~2.0B gross debt = 4.9% pre-tax, 5.75-5.80% notes issued 2024); market-value weights ~92% equity / 8% debt give ~9.2%. Rounded to 9.0% in recognition of the ~60% recurring consumables/parts/service revenue and 61 consecutive years of dividend growth, which place Nordson at the defensive end of capital-goods cyclicals. The same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality is charged once, in the bear path's FY2028 downturn, not again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: One treatment per lease class, each applied once. Operating leases (liability 68.5 at 2026-07-31; cash rent 19.5 in FY2025): treatment (B) - under ASC 842 the full operating-lease payment already sits inside operating cash flow and EBITDA, so no further charge is made and operating lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases (liability 18.7): treatment (A) - principal (5.6 in 9M FY2026) is a financing outflow outside the flows, so the liability is INCLUDED in total_debt. lease_cost_pct_path is therefore omitted.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. us-gaap:MinorityInterest is absent from the filings; all consolidated profit is attributable to Nordson shareholders.
inputs.ebitda_definition_note: ebitda_margin_path is PRE-SBC EBITDA (the engine deducts sbc_pct_path from it). FY2025 GAAP EBITDA = operating income 711.7 + depreciation 71.3 + intangible amortization 79.3 = 862.3 = 30.9% of revenue; 9M FY2026 = 586.7 + 109.4 = 696.1 = 31.25%. Adding SBC (0.8%) gives the ~32.1% FY2026E pre-SBC anchor. The Metrics CSV 'EBITDA' column (790.989 for FY2025) is operating income + intangible amortization only and omits depreciation, so it UNDERSTATES EBITDA by ~2.5pp of revenue; it is not used as the anchor. The company's own 'adjusted EBITDA' (~32-33%) additionally excludes restructuring/acquisition costs; the model stays on the GAAP basis so recurring one-offs are not silently added back.
inputs.da_capex_note: D&A runs ~4.9% of revenue (depreciation 2.3% + acquired-intangible amortization 2.6%) against capex of 1.8-2.4%. The model carries no future M&A, so amortization is tapered (4.8% -> 4.0%) as the Atrion/CyberOptics intangibles age. Because stock-deal amortization is largely non-deductible for cash tax, the cash tax rate is set at 23% rather than the ~21% GAAP/cash rate on EBIT (FY2025 taxes paid 147.9 / EBIT 711.7 = 20.8%, FY2024 23.8%) to offset the phantom tax shield the full-D&A tax base would otherwise create.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company, industrials row). First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry). Nordson is a diversified precision-dispensing/medical-components/test-and-inspection industrial with ~60% recurring revenue; deposits, AFFO, NAV and distress models are all inapplicable. Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - 0 interest income. FY0 is FY2026E at the guidance midpoint (fiscal year closes 2026-10-31, four weeks after valuation_date; the 10-K follows in December). The FY2026 anchor sits at a cyclical high for Advanced Technology Solutions (27% of revenue, organic +28-31% in Q3 on AI/semiconductor packaging), which is why the bear scenario carries an explicit FY2028 revenue decline and the bear weight is raised to 25%. Working capital: manufacturer with receivables + inventory well above payables (net operating working capital ~24% of revenue), so wc_capture_pct is NEGATIVE (-12%: growth consumes cash, a downturn releases it); FY2025's +66 release and FY2024's -66 build net to roughly zero, so -12% sits between the balance-sheet intensity and the observed neutrality. Terminal cap 18x owner FCF (below the 20x compounder default, above the 12-15x cyclical band) - Gordon at 9.0%/2.5% implies 15.8x so the cap does not bind in base or bear. Price is a regular-session close, not after-hours.

historical_growth.fcf_basis: owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (interest income not stripped, net-debt company): FY2020 439.0, FY2022 431.0, FY2025 642.2
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (5.65%, FY2020-FY2025, includes Atrion/CyberOptics M&A) cross-checked against the Ascend framework's 6-8% through 2029 (which also includes ~2-3pp of M&A). Base path starts at 8% (FY2027, backlog +35%) and decays to 3% by FY2036, averaging ~4.7% organic.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 11.6% exceeds revenue 5yr CAGR 5.65% by >30%: equity compounds on retained earnings at a ~35% payout and is not a growth signal for the business. EPS 3yr CAGR is -1.3% (FY2022 8.90 -> FY2025 8.56) because Atrion acquisition amortization and interest are in GAAP EPS; adjusted EPS grew. Revenue 3yr CAGR 2.5% reflects the FY2023-FY2025 semiconductor/electronics downcycle in ATS that FY2026 is now reversing.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs (14.2% 3yr, 7.9% 5yr) are ABOVE reported-FCF CAGRs because SBC fell from 30.7 (FY2022) to 18.9 (FY2025); SBC is shrinking as a share of cash flow, not growing. FY2025 FCF (661) includes a ~66 working-capital release and is 24% of the FY2022-FY2025 average; the model anchors FY0 on the component build (FY2026E owner FCF ~690-700), not on FY2025.

base.narrative: FY2027 +8% on the +35% backlog and ATS momentum, then organic growth decays through the Ascend 6-8% band (ex-M&A) to 3% by FY2036 as the AI packaging cycle matures and IPS reverts to mid-single digits. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin widens 90bp to 33% on MFS/ATS mix and NBS Next, then holds. D&A tapers as acquired intangibles age; capex 2.2%; cash tax 23%; growth consumes 12c of working capital per dollar of new revenue.

bull.narrative: The AI-infrastructure packaging cycle proves multi-year as management claims ('early stages'): ATS compounds high-teens for three years on Vantage XL / ExoSPHERE panel-level packaging and test & inspection, MFS sustains ~8% on Atrion cross-sell, and company growth runs 11% -> 7% through FY2030 before decaying to 3.5%. Mix shift lifts pre-SBC EBITDA to 34.5%. Terminal growth 3.0%. Same WACC - the upside is in the flows, not a cheaper discount rate.

bear.narrative: AI capex digests in 2027-28: ATS, 27% of revenue at a cyclical peak, falls ~25% in FY2028 (as electronics/semi equipment did in FY2009 and FY2023-24) while tariff escalation on China/Mexico/Canada sourcing compresses IPS margins faster than pricing recovers. Company revenue +3% in FY2027 on backlog, -6% in FY2028, then a slow 2-4% recovery; pre-SBC EBITDA troughs at 29.5% and rebuilds only to 31%. Working capital releases cash in the down year (negative capture on a negative change). Terminal growth 2.0%; WACC unchanged so the downturn is charged once.

scenario_narratives.base: Nordson exits FY2026 at the Ascend $3B milestone with a record backlog. Growth decelerates from 8% to 3% over ten years as the ATS semiconductor-packaging upcycle normalises and IPS tracks global industrial production at mid-single digits, while the MFS/ATS mix shift and NBS Next add ~90bp of EBITDA margin to 33%. No M&A is modelled; D&A tapers as acquired intangibles amortise off. Owner FCF margin runs ~22-23% of revenue throughout.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI infrastructure buildout (advanced/panel-level packaging, optical interconnect, test & inspection) is a multi-year cycle rather than a 2026 spike; ATS keeps compounding high-teens for three years and MFS sustains ~8% on Atrion. Revenue grows 11% -> 7% through FY2030 and pre-SBC EBITDA reaches 34.5% on mix. Terminal growth 3%.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI capex digests in FY2027-28 and ATS - a quarter of revenue at a cyclical peak - falls by a quarter in FY2028, as Nordson's electronics equipment lines did in FY2009 and FY2023-24. Tariff escalation across the ~67% non-US footprint compresses IPS margins. Revenue dips 6% in FY2028 and recovers at 2-4%; EBITDA troughs at 29.5% and rebuilds to 31%. The balance sheet (net debt ~2.3x owner FCF, investment-grade) carries no solvency risk, so this is an earnings-and-multiple bear, not a going-concern one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the FY2026 anchor is a record year with Advanced Technology Solutions (27% of revenue) growing 28-31% organically on an AI/semiconductor capex cycle that has reversed sharply twice in the last fifteen years (FY2009, FY2023-24), and because the Analysis JSON rates tariff exposure 'high' against a 67% non-US revenue base. Bull trimmed from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to hold - a multi-year AI packaging cycle, ATS margin durability at a record 27%, and MFS sustaining 8% post-Atrion - and management's 'early stages' framing is the company's own view, not evidence. Base at 50%: the ~60% recurring consumables/parts/service base and the Ascend track record make the middle path the most likely.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Nordson is a high-quality compounder (30%+ EBITDA margins, ~60% recurring revenue, 61 years of dividend growth) valued here on fully SBC-expensed owner free cash flow at a 9% USD WACC with a cyclical bear case explicitly in the flows. At the current price the market pays roughly 28-29x trailing owner FCF - an EV/FCF multiple the Gordon terminal value at 9%/2.5% (15.8x) does not reach even in the bull case, so the house value sits well below the price and the 15% hurdle entry price sits far below it. The gap is the price of the AI-packaging re-rating thesis, stated explicitly rather than buried in a terminal multiple. SBC is small (0.8% of revenue), so the house/street band is narrow and the valuation does not depend on SBC treatment.
key_risks_to_valuation: FY0 revenue is a cyclical high in Advanced Technology Solutions; if FY2026 proves the peak of the AI packaging cycle, the base path's 8%/6.5% FY2027-28 growth is too high and the bear path is the base
Tariff escalation on China/Mexico/Canada sourcing against a 67% non-US revenue base; pricing has offset costs so far but each round of escalation lags

No M&A is modelled: Nordson's Ascend 6-8% framework includes 2-3pp of acquisitions, so the model understates growth but also excludes the capital spent to buy it - value-neutral only if deals earn the WACC
Working-capital capture (-12%) and the 23% cash tax rate are judgment calls worth ~$5-8/share each in the base case
Terminal value is ~55-60% of enterprise value at a 9% WACC; a 1pp WACC move is worth ~$30-35/share
